_comment: Second, independent Logic App implementing docs/teams-concurrency-design.md step 4 (inbound human reply -> case resolution -> Foundry thread continuation -> nested Teams reply). Polls PER-CASE via Graph GET .../messages/{root-message-id}/replies, NOT the channel-level /messages/delta call - Graph's channel-level delta endpoint only returns TOP-LEVEL messages and never includes nested replies, so a channel-wide scan can never see follow-up questions. Instead, this workflow asks the Work IQ webapp for every open case tracked in CaseThreadMap (/list-open-cases), then polls each case's own /replies endpoint (/list-case-replies) and skips replies already marked processed (LastProcessedReplyId) or posted by the Agent Identity itself. Runs on its own recurrence, independent of the email-trigger workflow.json.

orchestratorAgentIdFilePlaceholder.defaultValue: <paste orchestrator_agent_id.txt content here, or resolve via Key Vault>

agentIdentityUserId._comment: Entra object id of the dedicated Agent Identity user (svc-fnol-agent) - used to filter out the agent's own Teams posts so the poller never reacts to its own case-alert/ack messages.

workiqApiKey._comment: Matches the WORKIQ_API_KEY app setting on app-autofnol-workiq.

Recurrence_poll_every_minute._comment: concurrency.runs=1 forces this trigger to run strictly one-at-a-time: if a poll cycle is still waiting on a Foundry follow-up run (Until_followup_run_completes, up to 10 min) when the next 30s recurrence fires, the new run is queued rather than started in parallel. This prevents two overlapping poller runs from both trying to POST a message to the same Foundry thread while a run is still active on it (400 'Can't add messages to thread while a run is active').

inputs._comment: Keep only replies NOT posted by the Agent Identity itself (avoid reacting to its own ack posts) AND newer than this case's LastProcessedReplyId (Teams message ids are monotonically increasing numeric-string timestamps, so a numeric comparison works as a simple watermark).
Continues the SAME Foundry thread mapped to this case - never a new/fresh thread - so the agent retains full case history per teams-concurrency-design.md step 6.

Validate_followup_run_completed._comment: Purely cosmetic/diagnostic: forces THIS action to show red/Failed in run history whenever the follow-up Foundry run's final status is anything other than 'completed' (e.g. 'failed', 'expired', 'cancelled', or the Until loop's own timeout), since Get_followup_run_status itself always shows Succeeded (the HTTP call worked - it's the payload's status field that indicates failure).

Get_followup_latest_message._comment: Also gated on Post_reply_to_Foundry_thread having actually Succeeded - runAfter conditions are AND'ed across dependencies, so if that action Failed (e.g. transient 401/403), everything downstream (Start_followup_run/Until_followup_run_completes/Validate_followup_run_completed) is Skipped and this action must NOT run either, otherwise it would fetch and repost the thread's STALE prior message instead of a real new answer.

inputs._comment: Nests the agent's follow-up answer under the ORIGINAL case root message, never as a new top-level message, keeping the whole case in one visually isolated Teams thread per teams-concurrency-design.md step 3.
Persists this reply's id as the case's new watermark so it is never reprocessed on a subsequent 30-second poll.
